documents.title: Statement on Guidance for the University of Pennsylvania Community on Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
documents.stance_why: The document opens with "Penn embraces innovations like generative artificial intelligence" and sets no ban or tiers, only conditions: disclose AI use, verify output, protect data. For coursework it says "Individual courses may have different or more narrow guidance" and asks educators to set clear guidelines, but the default is welcoming with conditions, so permit, not delegates.
documents.summary: Penn-wide guidance from Information Security and Privacy for faculty, staff and students on generative AI. It welcomes AI and sets principles of transparency, accountability, privacy, security and IP, then gives short advice for educators, students and researchers.

units.why: "Penn embraces innovations like generative artificial intelligence" states a welcoming default for AI in teaching and learning, so P02 (permit/encourage by default), addressed to all.
units.anchor: Penn embraces innovations like generative artificial intelligence

units.why: The scope sentence says what the document covers: "generative AI using large language models provided by third parties", a definition of scope, so P61.
units.anchor: scoped to generative AI using large language models provided by third parties

units.why: "should not be viewed as a final policy" and "will be updated regularly" say the guidance is provisional, so P54.
units.anchor: It is anticipated that this document will be updated regularly

units.why: "Be transparent about the use of AI. Disclose when a work product was created wholly or partially using an AI tool" is a disclosure requirement for everyone, so P24.
units.anchor: Disclose when a work product was created wholly or partially using an AI tool

units.why: "validate the accuracy of created content" and "wary of misinformation or hallucinations" tell users to verify AI output, so P31 (not P29, which is about owning submissions).
units.anchor: validate the accuracy of created content with trusted first party sources
units.frag_start: The user of AI should endeavor

units.why: "Users are accountable for their use of content created by AI" makes users responsible for AI-generated content they use, so P29.
units.anchor: Users are accountable for their use of content created by AI

units.why: "This can result in the production of biased and other unintended content" names the bias concern about AI, so P53 with modality informs.
units.anchor: result in the production of biased and other unintended content

units.why: "users of AI should avoid sharing personal or sensitive data with the tool" protects personal data because tools train on inputs, so P50.
units.anchor: users of AI should avoid sharing personal or sensitive data with the tool

units.why: Penn data of moderate or high risk may not be input without a contract and privacy and security review "as coordinated by Procurement"; this is institutional review of tools and data sharing, so P65 rather than P50.
units.anchor: A contract in place to protect Penn data
units.frag_end: when moderate or high-risk data is involved.
units.policy: Users should not input moderate or high-risk Penn data or intellectual property into an AI tool without a contract in place to protect Penn data and review by Penn's Privacy Office with consultation with the Office of Information Security.

units.why: "individual patient data and patient data sets (even if deidentified) may not be exposed to open or public AI tools" is a firm ban on patient data in public AI, so P50 with must-not.
units.anchor: may not be exposed to open or public AI tools or services, absent institutional approval

units.why: "new kinds of cyberattacks that are being used against AI users" when writing code tells users to be security-aware; nearest type is P75 though it is about attacks on AI users rather than phishing.
units.anchor: be aware of the new kinds of cyberattacks that are being used against AI users
units.frag_start: When using AI to write computer
units.fit_note: Concerns cyberattacks on users of AI-written code and AI-based technology, not AI-crafted phishing; also tells users to consult the security office.

units.why: "any data posted publicly will likely be scraped" warns about public data being used to train models; no type covers data scraping, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: any data posted publicly will likely be scraped and used in this way
units.frag_start: The rise of AI models has
units.uncovered_note: Warns users that publicly posted data is likely scraped to train AI models and that the legality of scraping is unresolved.

units.why: "adhere to established principles of respect for intellectual property, particularly copyrights" concerns copyright in building training datasets, so P52.
units.anchor: adhere to established principles of respect for intellectual property, particularly copyrights
units.frag_start: Members of the Penn community should

units.why: "Avoid uploading confidential and/or proprietary information to AI platforms" before patent protection is an IP-protection rule on what may be entered; P52 fits better than P20 (assignment specs) or P50 (personal data).
units.anchor: Avoid uploading confidential and/or proprietary information to AI platforms
units.fit_note: Rule is about preserving patent and copyright protection of unpublished IP, not licensing of AI output.

units.why: "oversight and review of the use of AI and verification of its outputs ... should be in place" governs AI in university operations, so P76.
units.anchor: oversight and review of the use of AI and verification of its outputs

units.why: "Use of AI should always be in alignment with Penn's Principles of Responsible Conduct" requires AI use to follow existing university conduct policy, so P77.
units.anchor: Use of AI should always be in alignment with Penn's

units.why: "it is important for instructors to provide students with clear guidelines ... on the use of AI within coursework" tells instructors to state AI expectations; P09 fits (syllabus or assignment statements) over P04 because the sentence is about communicating.
units.anchor: instructors to provide students with clear guidelines

units.why: "As expectations may vary between classes and instructors" says AI rules differ by instructor and class, leaving the decision to instructors, so P04.
units.anchor: expectations may vary between classes and instructors

units.why: "when and how the use of AI within a course should be cited" asks instructors to specify citation rules for AI, so P24 addressed to instructors.
units.anchor: when and how the use of AI within a course should be cited
units.fit_note: Addressed to instructors: they should define when and how AI use is cited, rather than students being told to disclose.

units.why: "Disclose to students when course materials have been created with the use of AI" is an instructor duty to disclose AI-made materials, so P48 (not P47, which is about instructor AI use in grading or feedback).
units.anchor: Disclose to students when course materials have been created with the use of AI

units.why: "and when AI detection software will be used in the course" is a separate duty: instructors tell students about detection tools they use; P47 (instructor disclosure of own AI use) is the closest.
units.anchor: when AI detection software will be used in the course
units.fit_note: Discloses use of AI detection software on students rather than instructor use of generative AI.

units.why: "Be aware of how AI tools may impact assignments and exams in your discipline" with a pointer to CETLI guidance asks instructors to inform themselves and be supported; P63.
units.anchor: Be aware of how AI tools may impact assignments and exams in your discipline
units.fit_note: Tells instructors to consider AI impact on assignments and exams and points to CETLI guidance; no workshops are described.

units.why: "All use of AI should be in line with Penn's Code of Student Conduct and the Code of Academic Integrity" ties student AI use to existing codes, so P77.
units.anchor: All use of AI should be in line with Penn's

units.why: "attributing AI created content to the specific AI tool and parameters used" describes citing the tool and settings, so P25; "may have" makes it informational.
units.anchor: attributing AI created content to the specific AI tool and parameters used

units.why: "Individual courses may have different or more narrow guidance on the use of AI that should be adhered to" makes students follow each course's rules, so P78 (not P11, which says one course does not bind others).
units.anchor: Individual courses may have different or more narrow guidance on the use of AI

units.why: "In the absence of other guidance, treat the use of AI as you would treat assistance from another person" is the AI-as-human-collaborator rule, so P45; it is not P06 because it names no ban.
units.anchor: treat the use of AI as you would treat assistance from another person

units.why: "it is also unacceptable to have AI to complete the task" forbids having AI do a task such as an essay when another person doing it would be unacceptable, so P19.
units.anchor: it is also unacceptable to have AI to complete the task
units.frag_start: this means if it is unacceptable

units.why: "having access to data is not the same as having permission to scrape the data or use it to train an AI model" restricts scraping data for training; P52 is nearest.
units.anchor: having access to data is not the same as having permission to scrape
units.frag_start: Keep in mind that having access
units.fit_note: About permission to scrape data and train models, not licensing of AI output.

units.why: "Consult with your department leadership and your discipline's publishing standards" on AI and authorship defers to venue and department rules for research, so P62.
units.anchor: Consult with your department leadership and your discipline's publishing standards

units.why: "Institutional Review Board approvals should be obtained prior to exposing research participant data" is a research rule on participant data, so P62.
units.anchor: Institutional Review Board approvals should be obtained prior to exposing research participant data
units.fit_note: Also a privacy rule on research participant data.

units.why: "Caution should be adopted when research involves the examination of high-risk data" including PII and participant health information in AI, so P50.
units.anchor: Caution should be adopted when research involves the examination of high-risk data

units.why: "Intellectual property law may limit what AI can be copyrighted or patented" and advice to consult the Penn Center for Innovation cover IP rights in research, so P52 (extending the general IP rule to researchers with added copyright and patent law).
units.anchor: Intellectual property law may limit what AI can be copyrighted or patented

units.why: "Researchers should reinforce with their mentees ... the appropriate use of AI" frames mentors as teaching responsible use, so P112.
units.anchor: Researchers should reinforce with their mentees
units.fit_note: Mentors reinforce appropriate AI use with mentees; not framed as modeling by example.

units.why: "This AI Guidance is largely focused on large language models" and its principles "apply generally to other machine learning and artificial intelligence technologies", which defines which AI is covered, so P61.
units.anchor: these principles apply generally to other machine learning and artificial intelligence technologies
units.frag_start: This AI Guidance is largely focused

units.why: "This Guidance applies to Penn faculty, staff, undergraduate students, pre-doctoral students, and post-doctoral trainees" states who the guidance binds, so scope, P61.
units.anchor: This Guidance applies to Penn faculty, staff, undergraduate students
units.fit_note: Defines the people covered rather than the AI covered.

units.why: "The Offices of Information Security and University Privacy developed this Guidance in collaboration with" other offices states how and by whom it was made, so P84.
units.anchor: developed this Guidance in collaboration with the Office of the Vice Provost for Education

units.why: "Schools, Centers, and other departments may publish more specific guidance on the use of AI" lets units set their own rules, so P85.
units.anchor: Schools, Centers, and other departments may publish more specific guidance

units.why: "For questions about educational policies, please contact the Vice Provost for Education" points to an office for questions on educational AI policy, so P80 (the other contacts are routing, coded with this one).
units.anchor: For questions about educational policies, please contact the Vice Provost for Education
units.fit_note: Lists contact offices for questions (education, research, procurement, IP, privacy, security, legal); does not say the offices enforce the policy.

documents.unit: Center for Excellence in Teaching, Learning and Innovation (CETLI)
documents.title: Creating AI Policies
documents.stance_why: The page says "Penn does not have a standardized policy on student AI use, and each instructor is responsible for setting their own guidelines" and then offers considerations and sample statements ranging from a full ban to open use. It sets no stance itself, so delegates.
tiers: Sample syllabus statement: no generative AI
Sample syllabus statement: AI allowed with attribution
Sample syllabus statement: any purpose if cited
Sample assignment policies: in-class secure browser no AI; AI not a scholarly source; required AI-Assisted Learning Disclosure
documents.summary: Teaching-center advice for instructors on writing course and assignment AI policies. It lists elements to consider (unauthorized assistance, sharing materials, citing AI) and sample syllabus and assignment language from banning to welcoming AI.

units.why: "Penn does not have a standardized policy on student AI use" states that no uniform policy exists, so P108.
units.anchor: Penn does not have a standardized policy on student AI use

units.why: "each instructor is responsible for setting their own guidelines" hands the decision to instructors, so P04.
units.anchor: each instructor is responsible for setting their own guidelines

units.why: "Your department or program may have recommendations or resources" notes units may add guidance beyond the considerations, so P85.
units.anchor: Your department or program may have recommendations or resources
units.fit_note: Units offer recommendations and resources for instructors rather than binding rules.

units.why: "The AI uses you allow or prohibit should reflect the kinds of thinking students need to do to achieve learning goals" ties permissions to learning goals, so P83.
units.anchor: should reflect the kinds of thinking students need to do to achieve learning goals

units.why: "Acceptable uses of AI are likely to differ by assignment, so you might consider creating AI policies that are specific to each assignment" is a per-assignment rule-setting recommendation, so P04.
units.anchor: you might consider creating AI policies that are specific to each assignment

units.why: "the impact of AI use will vary by task, enhancing some activities while hindering learning in others" asks that policies reflect each task; this follows learning goals, so P83.
units.anchor: enhancing some activities while hindering learning in others
units.fit_note: Task-level reasoning about whether AI helps or hinders learning.

units.why: "Communicate your policies early, often, and with explanation" tells instructors to explain reasons behind rules, so P66.
units.anchor: early, often, and with explanation.
units.frag_end: what they can and cannot do and why.

units.why: "Stating general policies in your syllabus as well as addressing specific expectations that pertain to individual assignments" asks for syllabus and assignment-level statements, so P09.
units.anchor: Stating general policies in your syllabus as well as addressing specific expectations
units.frag_end: can and cannot do and why.

units.why: "students may not use unauthorized assistance ... It is up to you to decide what that means" leaves the definition of unauthorized assistance to instructors, so P04.
units.anchor: It is up to you to decide what that means and communicate that definition
units.fit_note: Instructors define and communicate what counts as unauthorized assistance under the Code of Academic Integrity.

units.why: "some instructors may consider any significant use of AI to be an academic integrity violation, others may allow students to use AI in specific ways" describes the range of instructor stances, so P04.
units.anchor: others may allow students to use AI in specific ways or for particular parts

units.why: "Students might share course materials with AI tools to study" and the practice-quiz example describe allowable study uses of course materials, so P14.

units.fit_note: Also lists simplifying instructions and accommodations such as live notetaking.
